mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A sieve with holes larger than both flour and bran will still separate the flour from the bran.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: With holes between their sizes, fine flour remains on the sieve and bigger bran passes through.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Sieving removes dissolved salt from salt water.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Equal-sized pale sand grains pass through, but dark sand grains stay on the sieve.

intelligence.enrichment: Sieving allows smaller particles to pass through the holes of a sieve while bigger particles remain on the sieve. The size of the sieve holes relative to the particle sizes determines which particles pass through and which are retained. The learner correctly applies this rule: Sieving allows smaller particles to pass through the holes of a sieve while bigger particles remain on the sieve. A sieve keeps the wanted material on top, whatever its size is.
